proof: ResidualSplitCount returns an integer in [1, 100000]. Therefore total == entries means every accepted entry is already at one particle.
Increasing residualSplitK cannot lower a count below one. With unchanged Conz4d and active reference between planning and dispatch, stopping at this floor preserves every subsequent split count.
The mass-reference setup, K=10 reset, nonpositive budget/reference exits, zero-entry behavior and six-iteration maximum are unchanged.

Cancellation is checked before planning, within each Parallel.For row and after the join. A canceled partial count cannot trigger particle dispatch; Program.cs checks cancellation before ParallelTransientParticleDriver.
Entry counting uses thread-local accumulation and one extra Interlocked.Add per i-row. It adds no grid scan or allocation. Parallel.For joins before total and entries are tested.
performance_assessment: The normal one-scan path has a small added counting cost. The largest measured median difference was about 0.088 ms with four workers (9.4% of a sub-millisecond planner call); before/after ranges overlap. Avoid claiming zero overhead. Floor cases remove five unnecessary scans and measured about 83% less planner time.

integration.parallel_assessment: The maximum cross-build difference equals the after-build repeat spread and is consistent with parallel accumulation-order variation. Do not call the four-worker outputs byte-identical.

decision: The floor early exit is a minimal, behavior-preserving optimization with adequate targeted and combined evidence; no further source change or CPU test is needed.
